raw_output.raw_text: <search query="badminton tactical intention recognition singles deep learning" search_time="2026年5月10日10时27分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:108"><title>Strategy analysis of badminton players using deep learning from IMU and UWB wearables</title><summary>Badminton is a fast-paced sport that requires a high level of skill and coordination. To improve their skills, players can use activity trackers to monitor different shots and activities. These trackers utilize inertial measurement units (IMUs), which measures acceleration and angular velocity on the rackets, and the ultra-wideband (UWB) sensors, which measure the location of the player. This study first analyzes the use of UWB localization for tracking badminton players on the court and analyzes the location where shots are played. Furthermore, this study focuses on using both IMU at the racket and wrist and UWB sensors to recognize strategies utilized in badminton matches, employing convolutional neural network (CNN) and Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. The goal is to classify thirteen badminton shots, as well as an extra class that contains non-shot activities. The output of this shot classifier is provided to the strategy recognition model, which can identify four main strategies, with eleven variations in total, alongside an additional class designated for non-strategy instances such as movement or rest intervals. We trained and tested the models on data from six skilled badminton players. The best results were achieved by using both IMU and UWB data. The proposed 2D-CNN achieved a shot classification accuracy of 90.9%, while the proposed LSTM achieved a strategy recognition accuracy of 80%. The results of this study suggest that neural networks can be used to effectively classify badminton shots and strategies to improve the training of badminton players, as well as to analyze match data.</summary><hostname>imec</hostname><author_list><author name="Ben Van Herbruggen" affiliation="IDLab, department of information technology, Ghent University - imec" /><author name="Jaron Fontaine" affiliation="IDLab, department of information technology, Ghent University - imec" /><author name="Jonas Simoen" affiliation="IDLab, department of information technology, Ghent University - imec" /><author name="Lennert De Mey" affiliation="IDLab, department of information technology, Ghent University - imec" /><author name="Daniel Peralta" affiliation="IDLab, department of information technology, Ghent University - imec" /><author name="Adnan Shahid" affiliation="IDLab, department of information technology, Ghent University - imec" /><author name="Eli De Poorter" affiliation="IDLab, department of information technology, Ghent University - imec" /></author_list><url>https://imec-publications.be/bitstream/handle/20.500.12860/44188.3/8578_acc.pdf?sequence=2</url><publish_time>2024年7月5日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:109"><title>Implementation of GRU Model in Badminton Time Series Data for Movement Trajectory Prediction</title><summary>This study tackles the challenge of image recognition in badminton due to its small size and complex movement trajectory by developing a new dataset and predicting shot sequences. The experimental procedure involves two main steps: detailed pre-processing of original data (extracting key features, normalizing, and dividing into training and test sets) and using deep learning algorithms to predict future shots. We validated the model with 20 repeated experiments and multiple evaluation metrics (Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-Score) and confirmed statistical significance and stability through T-tests. The results demonstrate that the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) effectively predicts shot sequences, benchmarking with Long-Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Networks (1D-CNNs). The proposed architecture model with joint Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) achieved 59.77% accuracy compared to a random guessing baseline of 16.67%, showcasing superior performance and promising applications.

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="sports action prediction deep learning tennis badminton" search_time="2026年5月10日10时27分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:116"><title>Wearable Sport Activity Classification Based on Deep Convolutional Neural Network</title><summary>This paper develops a wearable sport activity classification system and its associated deep learning-based sport activity classification algorithm for accurately recognizing sport activities. The proposed wearable system used two wearable inertial sensing modules worn on athletes' wrist and ankle to collect sport motion signals and utilized a deep convolutional neural network (CNN) to extract the inherent features from the spectrograms of the short-term Fourier transform (STFT) of the sport motion signals. The wearable inertial sensing module is composed of a microcontroller, a triaxial accelerometer, a triaxial gyroscope, an RF wireless transmission module, and a power supply circuit. All ten participants wore the two wearable inertial sensing modules on their wrist and ankle to collect motion signals generated by sport activities. Subsequently, we developed a deep learning-based sport activity classification algorithm composed of sport motion signal collection, signal preprocessing, sport motion segmentation, signal normalization, spectrogram generation, image mergence/resizing, and CNN-based classification to recognize ten types of sport activities. The CNN classifier consisting of two convolutional layers, two pooling layers, a fully-connected layer, and a softmax layer can be used to divide the sport activities into table tennis, tennis, badminton, golf, batting baseball, shooting basketball, volleyball, dribbling basketball, running, and bicycling, respectively. Finally, the experimental results show that the proposed wearable sport activity classification system and its deep learning-based sport activity classification algorithm can recognize 10 sport activities with the classification rate of 99.30%.</summary><hostname>IEEE Xplore</hostname><publisher>IEEE Access</publisher><cite_count>23</cite_count><author_list><author name="Yu-Liang Hsu" /><author name="Hsing-Cheng Chang" /><author name="Yung-Jung Chiu" /></author_list><url>https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/8911315</url><publish_time>2019年11月25日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:117"><title>A Survey on Video Action Recognition in Sports: Datasets, Methods and Applications</title><summary>To understand human behaviors, action recognition based on videos is a common approach. In addition, the actions could be extremely fast and it becomes difficult to recognize them. In this paper, we present a survey on video action recognition for sports analytics. We introduce more than ten types of sports, including team sports, such as football, basketball, volleyball, hockey and individual sports, such as figure skating, gymnastics, table tennis, tennis, diving and badminton. Then we compare numerous existing frameworks for sports analysis to present status quo of video action recognition in both team sports and individual sports. Finally, we discuss the challenges and unsolved problems in this area and to facilitate sports analytics, we develop a toolbox using PaddlePaddle ¹, which supports football, basketball, table tennis and figure skating action recognition.</summary><hostname>arXiv</hostname><author_list><author name="Fei Wu" affil

Further, the collected data is preprocessed by employing uniform frame sampling and temporal noise filtering to preserve motion continuity and reduce estimation. Furthermore, human pose detection and estimation are performed using Media Pipe that assist to provide accurate 3Dimensional joint coordinates robustly from video frames. The global video editing software market is expanding rapidly, driven by the explosion of short-form video content across platforms like YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram, as well as corporate video demand and AI integration. Multiple credible sources converge on a market trajectory spanning 2024–2034:
- Valued at USD 3.5 billion in 2024, projected to reach USD 8.2 billion by 2034, with a CAGR of 8.9% (Reports and Data, 2025). <cite id="call_805732a14e99-0"></cite>
- IndustryResearch and Market Growth Reports indicate the market will surpass USD 15 billion by 2035 at a CAGR of ~8.7% (Global Growth Insights; Industry Research, 2026). <cite id="call_201b8f4be967-1"></cite><cite id="call_300326"></cite>
- Statista/Grand View Research-aligned forecasts project growth to USD 120 billion by 2030 at a CAGR of ~10.5% (Grand View Research; MarketsandMarkets, 2026). <cite id="call_9e75cde3525b-1"></cite><cite id="call_9e75cde3525b-0"></cite>
- A broader set of sources (including SNS Insider) reports the market was USD 3.09 billion in 2023 and will exceed USD 5.13 billion by 2032 at a CAGR of 5.8% (SNS Insider, 2024). <cite id="call_12eb6217ccc8-2"></cite>

Segmentation and drivers
- Professional video editing software held the largest segment in 2024, accounting for about 55% of the market (Market Research, 2025). <cite id="call_6dfa77db8511-3"></cite>
- Cloud-based editing tools and the surge in short-form video content are key growth drivers (DataIntelo, 2025). <cite id="call_42693896"></cite>
- The rise of video-as-a-service (EDaaS) and AI-powered editing features further propel demand; the global EDaaS market was valued at $450 million in 2023, with the video editing software market forecast to grow at a CAGR of 9.7% through 2027 (WorldMetrics, 2026). <cite id="call_9e75cde3525b-3"></cite>

Platform and regional insights
- Windows dominated the platform share in 2025 with 42.3%, while North America captured 38.4% of revenue. <cite id="call_300326"></cite>
- Android led mobile video editing apps in 2024 with 57.65% of the market share. <cite id="call_4345"></cite>

Market share of major products and ecosystems

Adobe (Premiere Pro, After Effects, and the broader Adobe Creative Cloud)
- Adobe Premiere Pro leads the professional video editing market with an estimated 35% share (ElectroIQ; SalesWhale, 2025). <cite id="call_77042ac5265c-1"></cite><cite id="call_f82801c1d627-0"></cite>
- Adobe’s ecosystem is dominant, with the company holding about 19% of the global video editor market and serving over 5 million professional users across 120 countries (Industry Research, 2025). <cite id="call_201b8f4be967-2"></cite>
- After Effects is a core motion graphics tool in Adobe’s suite and contributes significantly to Adobe’s market leadership; while specific After Effects market share is not quantified here, its integration with Premiere Pro and the broader Creative Cloud ecosystem reinforces Adobe’s dominance. <cite id="call_77042ac5265c-1"></cite><cite id="call_f82801c1d627-0"></cite>

CapCut (by ByteDance)
- CapCut is the fastest-growing and most downloaded video editing app globally, with over 1 billion downloads (Android only) and approximately 300 million monthly active users by late 2024. <cite id="call_9f41a5b5f022-3"></cite>
- In 2025, CapCut accounted for around 42% of the revenue generated by mobile video editing apps, underscoring its outsized influence in the consumer/micro-influencer and social media creator segments. <cite id="call_9f41a5b5f022-3"></cite>
- Mobile app download and usage data from 2025 shows CapCut captured 8.6% of all app downloads among the top 500 apps, far ahead of other editors. <cite id="call_9f41a5b5f022-0"></cite>
- Sensor Tower data (2025) highlights CapCut’s dominance in the “out-of-home” (global) market, with it and TikTok (ByteDance) capturing the top two spots in non-game app rankings by downloads and MAU. <cite id="call_9f41a5b5f022-2"></cite>

DaVinci Resolve (Blackmagic Design)
- DaVinci Resolve is a leading professional video editing and color-grading solution, with an estimated 15% market share among professional editors (ElectroIQ; SalesWhale, 2025). <cite id="call_77042ac5265c-1"></cite><cite id="call_f82801c1d627-0"></cite>
- It is particularly prominent for its Hollywood-grade color correction and a powerful free version, making it attractive across entry-to-mid-level professional workflows. <cite id="call_77042ac5265c-1"></cite><cite id="call_f82801c1d627-0"></cite>
- In industry reports, Adobe Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro, and DaVinci Resolve collectively account for about 68% of the professional non-linear editing market (China report, 2025). <cite id="call_5ec575ba1960-4"></cite>

Final Cut Pro (Apple)
- Final Cut Pro is the second-largest professional video editing software by share, with an estimated 25% in the professional market (ElectroIQ, 2025). <cite id="call_77042ac5265c-1"></cite>
- It leverages Apple Silicon (M1/M2) for superior performance, including faster rendering, export times, and buttery-smooth playback, which has strengthened its appeal among Mac users. <cite id="call_5ec575ba1960-2"></cite><cite id="call_5ec575ba1960-1"></cite>

Avid Media Composer
- Avid Media Composer is a trusted tool in film and TV production, with an estimated 10% market share among professional editors (ElectroIQ; China reports, 2025). <cite id="call_77042ac5265c-1"></cite><cite id="call_37a7c37b3369-0"></cite>
- It is widely used in broadcast and television, with strong penetration in China’s provincial-level+ television stations (83% in 2023). <cite id="call_37a7c37b3369-2"></cite>

Other notable players
- Filmora holds about 5% of the professional video editing market, targeting mid-level users who want quick, stylish edits. <cite id="call_f82801c1d627-0"></cite>
- iMovie and Vegas Pro each capture around 3% of the market, with iMovie focused on Apple users and Vegas Pro appealing to more serious editing workflows. <cite id="call_9f41a5b5f022-3"></cite>
- Pinnacle Studio targets beginners and intermediates with an intuitive, affordable suite, though professionals tend to favor more robust tools like Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve. <cite id="call_12eb6217ccc8-3"></cite>
- Corel VideoStudio represents less than 3% of professional workflows, with a strong presence in consumer markets due to its one-time purchase model and affordability. <cite id="call_d4fd874194ce-0"></cite>

Cloud-first and AI-powered tools
- Cloud-based editing tools are a major growth vector, with the cloud segment expected to expand rapidly alongside the broader market. <cite id="call_42693896"></cite>
- Generative AI in video editing is a fast-growing segment, valued at USD 0.9 billion in 2023 and projected to reach USD 4.0 billion by 2028 (CAGR ~38%), with key players including Runway ML, Magisto (a Vimeo company), Pictory, Lumen5, Rephrase AI, DeepBrain, and Animoto. <cite id="call_9e75cde3525b-1"></cite>
- Adobe has integrated AI features across its suite (Premiere Pro, After Effects), and DaVinci Resolve has also adopted AI-driven tools for tasks such as intelligent scene detection and color grading. <cite id="call_9e75cde3525b-1"></cite><cite id="call_f82801c1d627-0"></cite>

Market dynamics and outlook
- Growth drivers include the explosion of short-form video content, the proliferation of cloud-based editing tools, and rising demand from independent creators and enterprises (DataIntelo, 2025). <cite id="call_42693896"></cite>
- Challenges include intense competition, rapid technological change, risks associated with AI integration, and the accessibility of open-source alternatives (Market Research, 2025). <cite id="call_4345"></cite>
- The market is highly segmented by type (cloud-based, web-based, on-premise), application (commercial, personal), and region, with Asia-Pacific and North America leading in adoption and revenue. <cite id="call_300326"></cite><cite id="call_42693896"></cite>

In summary, the global video editing and creation software market is highly competitive and rapidly evolving, with Adobe leading the professional segment, CapCut dominating mobile-first editing among creators, and DaVinci Resolve and Final Cut Pro each holding strong positions on macOS and among professionals. Avid remains a trusted tool in broadcast and TV, while cloud-first and AI-powered platforms are reshaping workflows across the board. <cite id="call_77042ac5265c-1"></cite><cite id="call_9f41a5b5f022-3"></cite><cite id="call_f82801c1d627-0"></cite><cite id="call_5ec575ba1960-1"></cite><cite id="call_37a7c37b3369-0"></cite><cite id="call_9e75cde3525b-1"></cite></answer>

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="hollow motor shaft manufacturing electric motor shaft forging machining casting spun cup forming NEV" search_time="2026年5月10日10时25分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:1"><title>Spin Extrusion – A New Partial Forming Technology based on 7 NC-Axes Machining</title><summary>Hollow shape component approaches, applied to shafts and similar workpieces, represent a major potential for ground-breaking innovations in lightweight engineering and safety designs. Among suitable forming technologies, spin extrusion is a pioneering and particularly flexible hollow-shaping technique. All outside form elements, straight or stepped cylinders, cones or spherical rotation elements emerge just from the kinematics of tools. The inside hollow shapes, as e.g. circular cross-sections, shaft to collar connections such as spherical triangles, polygons, splines or dovetail forms are manufactured with a shaping mandrel. Spin extrusion can be applied first and foremost at dimensions that are unattainable with other techniques. The application includes hollow shafts, thick-walled cups and semi-finished tubular products that are not to be found in off-the-shelf cross-sections. In these cases the possibility for using of massive bars is connected with very high price advantages. Furthermore material-saving machining is attracting special attention for high-grade materials. The paper characterizes substantial steps of process analysis and the appliance of a new, derived from the bound method, numerical simulation method for spin extrusion process. Holistic process analysis is the prime factor for process capability. The specific application of the developed special methods of simulation, the accumulation of process data and the integrating into the Computer numerical control of spin extrusion machine is a precondition guaranteeing high-quality assurance.</summary><hostname>ScienceDirect</hostname><author_list><author name="R Neugebauer" affiliation="Fraunhofer Institute for Machine Tools and Forming Technology – Chemnitz, Germany" /><author name="R Glass" affiliation="Fraunhofer Institute for Machine Tools and Forming Technology – Chemnitz, Germany" /><author name="M Hoffmann" affiliation="Fraunhofer Institute for Machine Tools and Forming Technology – Chemnitz, Germany" /></author_list><url>https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0007850607600936</url></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:2"><title>METHOD OF MANUFACTURING A HOLLOW SHAFT HAVING A FLANGE AT ONE END THEREOF</title><summary>A method is required in which a plate-like flange member may be firmly secured at the front end of a hollow shaft member through a plastic working treatment by virtue of caulking combination, so as to manufacture a hollow shaft having a flange at one end thereof. In detail, the method comprises the steps of: preparing a plate-like flange member A having an axial projection 13 including a constricted portion 13a on one side thereof; preparing a hollow shaft member B having an elongate internal space arranged in the axial direction thereof; engaging the axial projection 13 of the plate-like flange member A into a front end portion of the hollow shaft member B and at the same time inserting a mandrel 15 into the hollow shaft member B; pressing the hollow shaft member B in its axial direction towards the plate-like flange member A while performing a shear spinning treatment on the outer periphery surface of the hollow shaft member B so that the hollow shaft member B is plastically deformed in its radial direction; engaging the front portion of the hollow shaft member B with the constricted portion 13a of the axial projection 13 of the plate-like flange member A by virtue of caulking combination.</summary><hostname>patentimages.storage.googleapis.com</hostname><author_list><author name="Shigeaki Yamanaka" affiliation="Hiroshima-ken (JP)" /><author name="Masami Oguri" affiliation="Tokyo (JP)" /></author_list><url>http://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/pdfs/US6959479.pdf</url><publish_time>2005年11月1日0时0分</publish_time></d

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="electric motor hollow shaft manufacturing spun cup forming spun forming hollow shaft automotive" search_time="2026年5月10日10时25分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:9"><title>Optimisation of processing routes for cross rolling and spin extrusion</title><summary>The trend towards lightweight construction in vehicle manufacturing results in an increased use of hollow shafts in vehicle gear boxes. In order to maintain their competitiveness producers have to reduce their costs and to improve the quality of their products permanently. This publication focuses on near-net-shape and net-shape forming of rotation-symmetrical workpieces by incremental rolling processes. Two methods, cross rolling and spin extrusion, which can be used combined or individually are described with a special focus on spin extrusion. raw_output.raw_text: <search query="electric motor rotor shaft hollow manufacturing flow forming flow forming hollow shaft automotive" search_time="2026年5月10日10时25分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:25"><title>Near net shape technology: An innovative opportunity for the automotive industry</title><summary>Near net shape is an innovative concept in industrial manufacturing. The main focus of this technology is to produce parts, as near as possible close to their final shape and contour, implementing non-chipping techniques. In this way the manufacturing gives the possibility of a finished product with minimal cutting. Near net shape technology also generates the opportunity to reduce the productive steps for a given process chain. Both the above-mentioned characteristics have the same main goal: achieving cost reduction. This fundamental target incorporates several other advantages, such as: reduction of process variability, quality improvement in the finished product and the possibility to focus the design of mechanical devices on functional features, eliminating technical constraints imposed by the process. Based on these factors and in cooperation with the IWU Fraunhofer Institut of Chemnitz, the authors conducted a research regarding the manufacturing of an innovative automotive gear shaft, produced by applying near net shape processes. The goal of this study is to evaluate whether it is more convenient to produce the part implementing a traditional production chain or an innovative one, based on near net shape techniques. The first step was to locate the available technologies in order to produce the selected part. There are two alternatives: a traditional cutting manufacture, performed with a numerical control turning machine and a near-net-shape technique, characterized only by deformation processes. The next step was to detect the main differential costs between the two opportunities. Comparing technical data and information available in literature, the authors detected the main differential voices of cost: raw material, amortization, manpower and direct setup. In order to make the study more reliable, the authors assumed an actual industrial environment, featured by an annual demand of 400,000 pieces and a product lifetime cycle of 10 yr. The evaluation led to the conclusion that the innovative manufacturing chain is more convenient.</summary><hostname>دانشیاری</hostname><publisher>Robotics and Computer-Integrated Manufacturing</publisher><author_list><author name="R Cominotti" affiliation="Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, University of Brescia, Viale Venezia 94, 25123 Brescia, Italy" /><author name="E Gentili" affiliation="Department of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, University of Brescia, Viale Venezia 94, 25123 Brescia, Italy" /></author_list><url>https://daneshyari.com/article/preview/413834.pdf</url><publish_time>2008年3月9日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:26"><title>Optimisation of processing routes for cross rolling and spin extrusion</title><summary>The trend towards lightweight construction in vehicle manufacturing results in an increased use of hollow shafts in vehicle gear boxes. raw_output.raw_text: <search query="automotive hollow shaft forging steel alloy grade" search_time="2026年5月10日10时25分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:61"><title>A finite element modeling method for predicting the cold radial forging quality of 20CrMnTiH hollow shaft: study of material composition and heat treatment parameters</title><summary><title>Abstract</title> Cold radial forging (CRF) is an efficient and high-precision process for manufacturing rotating parts such as axles and steering shafts. However, the extent of cold plastic deformation is limited in hot-rolled low-carbon steel. To maximize material performance and ensure the quality of CRF, in addition to improving the processing parameters, the alloy composition and heat treatment parameters must also be synergistically optimized. This study focused on the CRF process of 20CrMnTiH hollow shafts and established an evaluation system based on the residual stress, effective strain, and damage of the hollow shaft after processing. Furthermore, a finite element simulation model integrating Spheroidizing annealing (SA) and CRF was created using the phase diagram calculation method (CALPHAD). The feasibility of numerical simulations for SA and CRF was validated by Brinell hardness and residual stress experiments. Detailed analysis using variance analysis and Tukey's post-hoc test was conducted to examine the coupled effects of alloy composition, SA temperature (AT<sub>e</sub>), and SA time (AT<sub>i</sub>) on the forming quality. The results indicated that the significance of chemical composition and heat treatment parameters for hardness is Te > Mn, residual stress is Te > Mn > Cu > Ni > Si, effective strain is C > S > Ti > Si, and damage is C > Ti > Mn > AT<sub>i</sub> > Te. The optimal combination of chemical composition and heat treatment parameters was determined as 0.17%C-0.17%Si-0.93%Mn-0.035%P-1.15%(1.45%)Cr-0.1%Ti, AT<sub>e</sub>: 795℃ and AT<sub>i</sub>: 4h. For example, integration of contour conform cooling and lubrication channels into gear components can increase their service life and reduce lubricant consumption. Steels for quenching and tempering and case hardening steels are commonly used materials for gear components. However, the availability of these alloys for LPBF processing is still limited. In particular, the 30CrNiMo8 steel for quenching and tempering is frequently used for gear wheels. This specific alloy is largely unknown regarding the LPBF processing and remains challenging, because of its susceptibility to cracking and the high temperature gradients that occur during the LPBF process. Therefore, this study focuses on the LPBF processing of 30CrNiMo8 powder material including process parameter evaluation and material characterization. Additionally, effects of the heat treatment on the resulting microstructure and mechanical properties were investigated. Within this study the 30CrNiMo8 has been processed successfully with a density of well above 99.5% leading to promising mechanical properties. A more homogenous microstructure has been achieved with quenching and tempering, compared to the as-buld state.</summary><hostname>SpringerLink</hostname><publisher>Progress in Additive Manufacturing</publisher><author_list><author name="Livia Zumofen" affiliation="Centre for Product and Process Development, School of Engineering, Zurich University of Applied Sciences, Winterthur, Switzerland" /><author name="Andreas Kirchheim" /><author name="Hans-Jörg Dennig" /></author_list><url>https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s40964-020-00121-x.pdf?pdf=button</url><publish_time>2020年2月20日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:78"><title>Lightweight design and manufacturing of composites for high-performance electric motors</title><summary>The global demand for carbon saving and green mobility is changing propulsion systems from combustion engines to electric motors. Today, battery capacities are still low and the range of automotive vehicles needs to be improved. In this context, high-performance electric motors of high energy efficiency as well as low weight are gaining in importance. In the present paper, two approaches for reducing weight of electric motor rotors are presented. First, a lightweight approach comprising a hybrid shaft made of carbon reinforced plastic and stainless steel are outlined. It is manufactured by a novel process chain, where dry filament winding is combined with centrifugal casting. The steel inlays are joined in-mold during centrifugal casting. The second approach demonstrates the replacement of electric sheets by soft magnetic compounds (SMC, iron filled polyamide compound). These SMC parts are produced in an innovative two-component injection molding process. raw_output.raw_text: <search query="spun forming hollow shaft motor rotor NEV process" search_time="2026年5月10日10时25分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:92"><title>New warm forming processes to produce hollow shafts</title><summary>In order to maintain their competitiveness, the producers constantly have to reduce their costs and to improve the quality of their products. The trend towards lightweight construction in vehicle manufacturing results in an increased use of hollow shafts in vehicle gear boxes. The publication focuses on near-net-shape and net-shape forming of rotation-symmetrical workpieces by incremental rolling processes. Two methods, cross rolling and spin extrusion, which can be used combined or individually are described. In addition an approach to experimental methods for determination of local forming parameters and different simulation methods will be included.</summary><hostname>ScienceDirect</hostname><publisher>Journal of Materials Processing Technology 119 (2001) 277-282</publisher><author_list><author name="R Neugebauer" affiliation="Fraunhofer Institute for Machine Tools and Forming Technology Chemnitz, Chemnitz, Germany" /><author name="M Kolbe" /><author name="R Glass" /></author_list><url>https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924013601009396</url><publish_time>2001年1月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:93"><title>NEW TECHNOLOGIES IN MANUFACTURING</title><summary>Abstract—for manufacturing thin-walled shafts for gas turbine engines of heat-resistant steels and alloys, the labor-intensive multistage drawing of a sheet of the workpiece in dies is used. The following problem is posed in the work: to study the possibility of manufacturing such parts by a less labor-intensive method: the rotary drawing of a thick-walled workpiece (sheet) by a spinning lathe by rolling a roll under hot deformation conditions. <answer>Could you provide information on recent developments in cloud-based train control systems for urban rail transit? I'm also interested in understanding the key technologies involved?

Below is a well-structured, data-driven report on recent developments and core technologies in cloud-based train control systems for urban rail transit.

Recent developments
- Live deployments of cloud-ready CBTC in metro operations:
  - Siemens Mobility has completed a live demonstration of its Signaling X solution in a metro system, integrating CBTC, interlocking, ATS, ATO, and SCADA into a centralized “signaling data center” architecture. Safety-critical functions run on commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) hardware via the DS3 platform, achieving claimed operational efficiency gains of up to 20% and energy savings of up to 30%, with SIL4 safety assurance. <cite id="call_1eb0079e8d48-1"></cite><cite id="call_84e077c333cf-0"></cite>
- Next-generation CBTC with AI, 5G, and cloud integration:
  - Hitachi Rail is advancing its SelTrac (G9) CBTC system to incorporate AI, 5G communications, and cloud computing, targeting deployment in Canadian and global urban rail networks to reduce costs and improve passenger experience. <cite id="call_1eb0079e8d48-2"></cite>
- China’s rapid adoption and innovation:
  - China’s urban rail transit mileage surpassed 10,000 km globally in 2023, with the intelligent systems market expanding at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12.5% (2021–2022) and projected to exceed CNY60 billion by 2025 (CAGR ~15–20%). <cite id="call_7cd9e7308f25-3"></cite><cite id="call_476bbf594705-0"></cite>
  - Multiple vendors and research institutes have demonstrated cloud-native signaling:
    - Enrite’s “信创安全云列车运行控制系统” (cloud-based train control system) passed field testing in early 2025, aligning with CBTC and FAO safety standards and moving toward full system cloudification. <cite id="call_2d6ec32c12cd-0"></cite>
    - China Communications Construction Co. (China通号) introduced a “云—端” (cloud–edge) signaling system that digitizes trackside devices, centralizes logic on the cloud, and provides station- and center-level control, improving scalability and efficiency. <cite id="call_2d6ec32c12cd-1"></cite>
    - China Urban Rail Transit Association–approved projects have spurred “云+边缘” (cloud plus edge) architectures and signaling-as-a-service models, with vendors targeting full-stack国产化 (indigenous) solutions. <cite id="call_2d6ec32c12cd-0"></cite><cite id="call_2d6ec32c12cd-3"></cite>
  - Emerging cloud-native signaling concepts:
    - A novel “software-defined train control” (SDTC) architecture proposed in 2022 moves core functions (including onboard controllers) to the cloud, leaving only sensors and I/O on trackside and trains, enabling scalable, service-oriented signaling. <cite id="call_1eb0079e8d48-3"></cite>
    - A 2025 CICTP paper outlines a “dual safety-oriented” cloud signaling system for urban rail, designed to meet functional safety and performance requirements while advancing smart urban rail digitalization. <cite id="call_c95414cda694-2"></cite>
- Market and operator trends:
  - Industry surveys indicate strong adoption of AI-driven diagnostics (~61%) and cloud-integrated monitoring (~58%) in train control management systems, with Asia-Pacific holding ~39% of the market and Europe ~27%. <cite id="call_7cd9e7308f25-0"></cite>
  - Digital twin integration and cloud platforms are expanding, with market value projected to grow from ~US$1.36 billion in 2024 to ~US$3.5 billion by 2029 at a CAGR of 20.8%, driven by real-time data integration and sustainability goals. <cite id="call_84e077c333cf-3"></cite>
- Cybersecurity and resilience:
  - Research has addressed cybersecurity in train-to-train (T2T) CBTC under jamming attacks and proposed multi-agent deep reinforcement learning strategies to maintain safety-critical operations. <cite id="call_c95414cda694-3"></cite>
  - Cloud-specific safety measures include independent “third-party” edge nodes for monitoring cloud-executed safety logic and hybrid cloud–edge communication frameworks to reduce latency and improve reliability. <cite id="call_c95414cda694-0"></cite><cite id="call_84e077c333cf-2"></cite>

Key technologies
- Cloud-native and hybrid cloud–edge architectures:
  - Cloud-centric signaling data centers consolidate CBTC, interlocking, ATS, ATO, SCADA, and other subsystems on COTS hardware with SIL4 safety assurance, enabling centralized management, easier upgrades, and energy savings. <cite id="call_84e076f333cf-0"></cite><cite id="call_84e077c333cf-2"></cite>
  - Hybrid cloud–edge frameworks deploy edge servers per rail line to handle real-time control (e.g., model predictive tracking) while the cloud manages orchestration across the network, reducing latency for safety-critical functions and enabling rapid fault isolation and rerouting. <cite id="call_84e077c333cf-3"></cite><cite id="call_476bbf594705-4"></cite>
  - Software-defined train control (SDTC) proposals move onboard controllers and logic to the cloud, retaining only sensors and I/O on trains and trackside, to support scalable, service-oriented signaling. <cite id="call_1eb0079e8d48-3"></cite>
- High-speed, low-latency communications:
  - 5G is increasingly used to connect trains to cloud/edge controllers, enabling faster data transfer and supporting T2T communications that simplify network topologies and reduce delays. <cite id="call_84e077c333cf-2"></cite><cite id="call_c95414cda694-3"></cite>
- Safety and certification:
  - Safety Integrity Level 4 (SIL4) assurance is achievable on COTS hardware via platforms like DS3, with independent edge monitoring to ensure cloud-executed safety logic meets EN 50129 and other rail safety standards. <cite id="call_84e077c333cf-2"></cite><cite id="call_c95414cda694-0"></cite>
- AI and data analytics:
  - Deep learning models for train headway prediction improve dispatch decision-making by capturing spatiotemporal dependencies across entire metro lines. <cite id="call_4292ef837a6e-2"></cite>
  - Computer vision (e.g., Mask R-CNN, YOLOv8) achieves high wear/damage detection performance (mIoU up to 0.9564), supporting predictive maintenance. <cite id="call_4292ef837a6e-3"></cite>
  - Explainable ML pipelines provide natural language and visual explanations for fault prediction in metro operators’ data streams. <cite id="call_4292ef837a6e-4"></cite>
  - Multi-agent reinforcement learning mitigates jamming in T2T-CBTC to preserve safety-critical operations. <cite id="call_c95414cda694-3"></cite>
- Energy optimization:
  - Energy-optimal timetable design and rolling MPC optimize regenerative braking utilization and traction energy, with field trials reporting traction energy reductions of ~0.95% and regenerative braking increases of ~8.18%. <cite id="call_0326acea52c3-1"></cite><cite id="call_0326acea52c3-3"></cite>
- Predictive maintenance and anomaly detection:
  - Hybrid unsupervised clustering and spectral analysis detect track anomalies in real time from onboard sensors, improving defect identification beyond traditional periodic inspections. <cite id="call_4292ef837a6e-1"></cite>
  - Multi-sensor fusion (vibration, temperature, current, vision) with small-sample learning and explainable AI enables precise anomaly detection and remaining useful life prediction in rolling stock. <cite id="call_4292ef837a6e-4"></cite>
- Digital twin and cloud integration:
  - Integrated cloud–edge–digital-twin platforms enable perception–fusion–prediction/optimization–execution feedback loops, supporting AI-driven scheduling and real-time strategy execution. <cite id="call_84e077c333cf-4"></cite>
  - Cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, Azure) provide scalable, secure infrastructure for digital twin platforms and large-scale data processing, reducing on-premises maintenance. <cite id="call_4292ef837a6e-4"></cite>
- Edge computing for real-time control:
  - Edge computing addresses real-time constraints in train control by processing data near the source, reducing latency and enabling local decision-making (e.g., automatic signal adjustments, rapid fault isolation). <cite id="call_476bbf594705-4"></cite>
- Cybersecurity:
  - Intrusion detection systems on trains analyze mobility data to detect attacks on traction and braking commands, enhancing resilience. <cite id="call_c95414cda694-4"></cite>
  - Redundant communication protocols and independent edge monitoring strengthen resilience against jamming and other cyber threats. <cite id="call_c95414cda694-3"></cite><cite id="call_c95414cda694-0"></cite>

Outlook
- Architectural convergence:
  - Cloud-native, hybrid cloud–edge, and software-defined signaling are converging toward centralized cloud data centers with localized edge processing, enabling signaling-as-a-service, faster upgrades, and energy savings while maintaining SIL4 safety. <cite id="call_84e077c333cf-2"></cite><cite id="call_1eb0079e8d48-3"></cite><cite id="call_c95414cda694-2"></cite>
- AI integration deepens:
  - Predictive maintenance, energy-optimal scheduling, and dispatch decision-making will expand with more data fusion, explainable AI, and reinforcement learning, supported by digital twin platforms. <cite id="call_4292ef837a6e-3"></cite><cite id="call_4292ef837a6e-2"></cite><cite id="call_4292ef837a6e-4"></cite><cite id="call_84e077c333cf-4"></cite>
- Communications evolve:
  - 5G and T2T-CBTC will reduce network complexity and latency, with cybersecurity measures (IDS, jamming resilience, secure protocols) becoming central to design. <cite id="call_84e077c333cf-2"></cite><cite id="call_c95414cda694-3"></cite><cite id="call_c95414cda694-4"></cite>
- Regional momentum:
  - China’s metro expansion and policy support (e.g., ISCS cloud guidance) are accelerating cloud-native signaling, with vendors and research institutes demonstrating hybrid cloud–edge, SDTC, and dual-safety cloud signaling. <cite id="call_7cd9e7308f25-3"></cite><cite id="call_2d6ec32c12cd-0"></cite><cite id="call_2d6ec32c12cd-1"></cite><cite id="call_c95414cda694-2"></cite>
- Cloud infrastructure maturation:
  - Adoption of cloud platforms (AWS, Azure) and data integration tools (Apache Kafka) will continue to lower infrastructure costs and improve scalability for digital twin and analytics workloads. <cite id="call_4292ef837a6e-4"></cite>

In summary, cloud-based train control for urban rail transit is transitioning from traditional CBTC toward cloud-native, hybrid cloud–edge architectures that leverage AI, 5G, and digital twins, with strong momentum in Asia-Pacific markets and growing emphasis on safety, cybersecurity, and energy efficiency. <cite id="call_84e077c333cf-2"></cite><cite id="call_1eb0079e8d48-3"></cite><cite id="call_7cd9e7308f25-0"></cite><cite id="call_84e077c333cf-3"></cite><cite id="call_c95414cda694-2"></cite></answer>

The high communication delay between trains and the ground control centers is a crucial challenge when deploying autonomous train control with the existing train...
To tackle the challenges, we propose a 5G-based collaborative cloud and edge communication framework to provide the communication and computation infrastructure for autonomous train control. We deploy one edge server for each rail line, and the edge server only provides computation service for the trains on the related line. The cloud server manages all edge servers and implements tasks for all the equipment in the system.

problem: Please draft a research report analyzing future product development trends within the smart home industry. The report should conclude by identifying specific types of products, or products with particular features, that are expected to be major trends shaping the industry's future.
final_response:
<think>
We have already gathered market growth figures (Statista-style forecasts), interoperability trends (Matter adoption, standards discussions), privacy/user experience findings, AI integration in homes, aging-in-place technologies, energy efficiency and grid interaction, voice assistants/ecosystem growth, and regulatory/compliance impacts. The “major trends shaping the industry’s future” should be concise product/theme categories with brief rationales tied to the above sources. Avoid unsupported specifics; use citations for each claim.
</think>

<answer>Below is a data-driven analysis of future product development trends in the smart home industry, concluding with specific product types and features expected to be major trend drivers.

Market and adoption context
- Global smart home market size is forecast to grow at a compound annual rate (CAGR) of around 10–13% through 2028, reaching approximately $173 billion (USD) or €87 billion+ in select regions, with strong growth in Asia and Europe, reflecting broad geographic momentum. <cite id="call_70447fa092cf-1"></cite><cite id="call_70447fa092cf-3"></cite>

Key development themes
1. Interoperability-first ecosystems
- The Matter protocol has accelerated cross-platform compatibility, with over 10,000 certified products across 25+ categories and strong platform integration (Apple HomeKit, Google Home, Amazon Alexa, Samsung SmartThings) by early 2024, alongside rising consumer awareness and logo recognition. <cite id="call_5b7cb8aa84e5-0"></cite><cite id="call_5b7cb8aa84e5-3"></cite>
- Industry-wide interoperability efforts are reducing fragmentation and improving user retention and satisfaction, a core enabler for broader product adoption. <cite id="call_541e8b354e68-1"></cite>

2. Privacy-centric design and control
- Privacy-conscious users report complex and often confusing technical landscapes around data flows and access, underscoring a need for transparent, user-aligned privacy tools and controls. <cite id="call_0a66565c57e2-0"></cite>
- Legal frameworks such as the GDPR are reshaping compliance expectations in smart buildings and homes, requiring clearer definitions of “personal data,” individual rights, and DPIA practices. <cite id="call_5a08ec92e3bb-1"></cite>

3. Artificial intelligence for personalization and autonomy
- AI/ML is enabling proactive assistants and energy management, with studies showing nudges from voice assistants can influence occupant behavior (e.g., energy savings), and machine learning classifiers achieving high accuracy in detecting malicious activity in smart home networks. <cite id="call_7e4757e4cf7f-0"></cite><cite id="call_eda340e7c827-0"></cite>
- Comprehensive reviews indicate AI is central to services, automation, and security, with clear trends toward context-aware, adaptive systems. <cite id="call_fef3662a293a-0"></cite><cite id="call_21e6c7525d2a-0"></cite>

4. Aging populations and aging-in-place
- Digital health and wearables are pivotal for healthy aging, with remote monitoring and assistive technologies helping older adults maintain independence at home. <cite id="call_4eb8af5c84ee-0"></cite>
- In China, AI-enabled older adult care is expanding into health monitoring, smart home integration, emotional companionship, and medical services, with proposed pathways emphasizing user experience, privacy, and standardization. <cite id="call_4eb8af5c84ee-1"></cite>

5. Energy efficiency and grid interaction
- Electrification of homes and transportation (EVs) is driving demand for integrated energy management, with studies showing that pairing rooftop solar with EV charging and using EMS can reduce emissions and stabilize grids, and bidirectional charging (V2G/G2V) is emerging as a key capability. <cite id="call_21e6c7525d2a-0"></cite>
- Intelligent coordination of distributed energy resources is essential for decarbonization and clean energy deployment, linking smart home energy systems to broader grid strategies. <cite id="call_21e6c7525d2a-1"></cite>

6. Voice and conversational interfaces
- Voice assistants have become a dominant interface for smart home control, with smart speaker shipments surpassing 300 million globally by 2024 and over 65% of voice searches routed through smart speakers, highlighting their centrality in daily interactions. <cite id="call_ee0c5783ca53-1"></cite><cite id="call_ee0c5783ca53-2"></cite>
- Voice-based assistants are increasingly proactive, improving user experience and energy outcomes through conversational control and personalized suggestions. <cite id="call_7e4757e4cf7f-0"></cite>

Major product types and features expected to shape the industry
- Matter-certified, cross-ecosystem hubs and edge hubs with local processing and security (IDS, segmentation) to reduce reliance on centralized clouds, improve privacy, and strengthen network resilience. <cite id="call_5b7cb8aa84e5-0"></cite><cite id="call_eda340e7c827-0"></cite><cite id="call_3f875a0a2d88-0"></cite>
- Privacy-first smart home hubs and gateways that localize data and provide granular user controls, aligning with user-reported complexity in data flows and GDPR compliance requirements. <cite id="call_0a66565c57e2-0"></cite><cite id="call_5a08ec92e3bb-1"></cite>
- AI-native assistants and services that deliver proactive suggestions and adaptive automation (e.g., energy and comfort), supported by knowledge-driven security and machine learning-based threat detection. <cite id="call_fef3662a293a-0"></cite><cite id="call_21e6c7525d2a-0"></cite><cite id="call_eda340e7c827-0"></cite>
- Integrated energy and EV ecosystems (solar + storage + EV charging) with grid-interactive capabilities (V2G/G2V) to reduce emissions, optimize costs, and support grid stability, reflecting decarbonization imperatives and intelligent electrification. <cite id="call_21e6c7525d2a-0"></cite><cite id="call_21e6c7525d2a-1"></cite>
- Voice-first control centers (smart speakers and displays) that unify multi-modal interactions and serve as the primary interface for home automation, security, and entertainment, leveraging high adoption rates and conversational capabilities. <cite id="call_ee0c5783ca53-1"></cite><cite id="call_ee0c5783ca53-2"></cite><cite id="call_7e4757e4cf7f-0"></cite>
- Aging-in-place technologies that combine wearables, health monitoring, fall detection, emergency response, and ambient assistance (e.g., smart lighting, medication reminders) to support independent living and align with demographic trends and regulatory focus on privacy and standards. <cite id="call_4eb8af5c84ee-0"></cite><cite id="call_4eb8af5c84ee-1"></cite>

Conclusion
The smart home industry is converging around interoperable, privacy-aware platforms powered by AI and voice-first interfaces, while aging-in-place and energy efficiency are driving specialized, integrated solutions. Products and features that deliver cross-ecosystem compatibility, localized data control, proactive assistance, grid-interactive energy management, and assistive aging capabilities are poised to be major trend drivers in the coming years. <cite id="call_5b7cb8aa84e5-0"></cite><cite id="call_0a66565c57e2-0"></cite><cite id="call_fef3662a293a-0"></cite><cite id="call_21e6c7525d2a-0"></cite><cite id="call_ee0c5783ca53-1"></cite><cite id="call_4eb8af5c84ee-0"></cite></answer>

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="smart home market size forecast 2024-2028 CAGR report" search_time="2026年5月10日10时29分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:27"><title>From Internet of Things to System of Systems: Market analysis, achievements, positioning and future vision of the ECS community on IoT and SoS</title><hostname>Eurotech</hostname><publisher>An ARTEMIS-IA Whitepaper</publisher><author_list><author name="Paolo Azzoni" affiliation="EUROTECH Group" /></author_list><url>https://www.eurotech.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/06/From-Internet-of-Things-to-System-of-Systems.pdf</url><publish_time>2020年4月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:28"><title>Internet of Things Technology in Home Marketing under Intelligent Environment</title><summary>With the improvement of per capital consumption level, the rapid development of Internet of things and artificial intelligence technology, and the continuous change of people's life style caused by technological changes, the smart home industry will shine brilliantly in the future market. The purpose of this research is to apply the Internet technology of mono to marketing of modern smart home market. This study analyzes the sales situation of smart homes in the market for the last three years as an experimental data and analyzes the areas of smart home that consumers prefer and the areas that need to be improved. In this study, we combine intelligent data processing technology of the Internet and rationalize the acquired data and predict and plan the future development of the smart home industry. It uses the Internet, big data, and other networks to effectively diffuse and find potential users of smart home. The research results show that the average annual growth rate of China's smart home market is 20%, and the industry output value will reach 96 billion yuan in 2019. It is estimated that the annual growth rate will reach about 25% from 2022 to 2035, and the channel growth will be 27% in 2019. In terms of furniture selection, 44% of consumers pay attention to the design and appearance of furniture, exceeding the proportion of paying attention to material and workmanship. The results show that the smart home industry is developing continuously and more and more consumers pay attention to the smart home industry. The conclusion is that the data processing of Internet of things technology accurately and efficiently analyzes the current situation of consumers' preferences and potential customers for smart home, which contributes to the development and planning of the company's marketing.</summary><hostname>Clausius Scientific Press Inc</hostname><publisher>Information Systems and Economics</publisher><author_list><author name="Lai-Wang Wang" affiliation="Department of Industrial Engineering and Management, National Kaohsiung University of Science and Technology, Kaohsiung City, 807618, Taiwan" /><author name="Chen-Chih Hung" affiliation="Minjiang University, Fuzhou, 350108, China" /><author name="Haoming Wen" affiliation="Department of International Business, National Kaohsiung University of Science and Technology, Kaohsiung City, 824004, Taiwan" /><author name="Ching-Tang Hsieh" affiliation="Department of International Business, National Kaohsiung University of Science and Technology, Kaohsiung City, 824004, Taiwan" /></author_list><url>http://166.62.7.99/assets/default/article/2022/03/26/article_1648286893.pdf</url></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:29"><title>BUSINESS MODEL DESIGN FOR A FIRM OPERATING IN A SMART HOME MARKET</title><hostname>Repozitorij Univerze v Ljubljani</hostname><publisher>UNIVERSITY OF LJUBLJANA SCHOOL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS</publisher><author_list><author name="Jaka Koak" affiliation="UNIVERSITY OF LJUBLJANA SCHOOL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS" /><author name="Karin Mohar" affiliation="UNIVERSITY OF LJUBLJANA SCHOOL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS" /></author_list><url>https://repozitorij.uni-lj.si/IzpisGradiva.php?id=132676</url><publish_time>2021年8月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:30">

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="global smart home market to reach USD 173 billion by 2028 CAGR 13.9 Statista 2024" search_time="2026年5月10日10时29分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:35"><title>JOURNAL OF NONLINEAR ANALYSIS AND OPTIMIZATION: THEORY & APPLICATIONS</title><publisher>Vol-15 No-1 Special Issue-03 (April 2024) UGC CARE Journals</publisher><url>http://202.88.229.59:8080/jspui/bitstream/123456789/5726/1/JNAO%20Theory%20and%20Applications.pdf</url><publish_time>2024年4月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:36"><title>Editorial – Special Issue: Managing Smart Services and Smart Service Systems</title><summary>Smart services are becoming increasingly present in our daily lives. The number of digital voice assistants (e.g., Amazon’s Alexa and Apple’s Siri) used in devices worldwide is expected to rise from 4.2 billion units in 2020 to 8.4 billion in 2024 (Laricchia 2022a), and the global voice recognition market is forecast to grow from USD 10.7 billion in 2020 to USD 27.2 billion by 2026 (Thormundsson 2022). The number of smart homes in Europe is expected to grow from 18.3 million in 2020 to 94.8 million in 2026, and the global revenue for the smart home market is expected to reach more than USD 200 billion in 2026 (Lasquety-Reyes 2021). Moreover, 30% of Germans use smart watches or health/fitness trackers (this percentage is about the same for US citizens but less than reported for citizens of India, where usage is 41%), and smart-watch market revenue worldwide is expected to grow to USD 59 billion in 2026 (Laricchia 2022b). This list of illustrative examples could be extended considerably, clearly indicating that smart services and smart service systems are finding their way into most industries and areas of life. Smart services are delivered to or through smart products (e.g., Allmendinger and Lombreglia 2005; Wünderlich et al. 2015), which consist of both tangible (i.e., hardware) and intangible (i.e., software) components (Raff et al. 2020). A smart service system, in turn, is a configuration of smart products and service providers that offer smart services (e.g., Beverungen et al. 2019; Henkens et al. 2021). The advent of smart services and smart service systems has challenged both companies and competition (Porter and Heppelmann 2014, 2015). On the one hand, we find completely new providers of smart services, frequently in the form of startups or corporate spin-offs, entering the market with new service offerings (e.g., app-Wash, a spin-off of Miele, offering a digital service for laundry rooms; Kaiser et al. 2022). On the other hand, we find traditional companies enhancing their formerly non-smart products or services by incorporating smart capabilities (see, e.g., Klos et al. 2023 (forthcoming)). As a result, even in a traditional sector such as agriculture, the vast majority of German farmers today use digital technologies or applications, such as GPS-controlled agricultural machinery, smart feeding systems, or smart systems, for the site-specific application of crop protection agents or fertilizers (Bitkom 2020). The corresponding digital transformation is perhaps the most pervasive managerial challenge for companies (Nadkarni and Prügl 2021). Whether it is a startup or incumbent firm, all market actors find the core elements of their company’s business model challenged in the rising era of smart services and service systems (Beverungen et al. 2019). With this special issue, we seek to shed further light on the challenges and managerial implications arising from the transition toward smart service (systems), which could be mapped to a simplified version of the CANVAS business model (Osterwalder et al. 2005, see Figure 1). Specifically, we consider (1) the value proposition, (2) the customer side, (3) the required company infrastructure, and (4) the financial aspects. Additionally, the special issue links the business model to challenges driven by external factors, such as changes to the legal framework.</summary><hostname>ResearchGate</hostname><publisher>Journal of Service Managem

raw_output.raw_text: <search query="smart home adoption growth 2020 2026 Europe 94.8 million Statista Market Forecast" search_time="2026年5月10日10时29分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:43"><title>Smart Home Adoption: Diffusion Prospects of the Smart Home and Voice as a Mean of Control in Sweden</title><hostname>DiVA Portal</hostname><publisher>KTH ROYAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY</publisher><author_list><author name="Madeleine Gartz" affiliation="KTH ROYAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY SCHOOL OF INDUSTRIAL ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT" /><author name="Ida Linderbrandt" affiliation="KTH ROYAL INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY SCHOOL OF INDUSTRIAL ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT" /></author_list><url>https://www.diva-portal.org/smash/get/diva2:1372032/FULLTEXT01.pdf</url><publish_time>2019年1月1日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:44"><title>FIVE PRIORITIES FOR ACHIEVING EUROPE'S DIGITAL SINGLE MARKET</title><summary>The EUROPEAN UNION HAS set out ambitious digital goals in its vision for a Digital Single Market (DSM)—and with good reason. The EU’s Internet economy contributes some €700 billion a year, or 5 percent, to GDP, and the high-tech sector employed almost 8.5 million people in 2013 (almost 4 percent of total employment). The potential economic impact is even greater. The next wave of growth will be propelled by the Internet of Things (IoT), which is expected to contribute almost €330 billion of new revenues in Europe by 2020. The rise of voice-based virtual assistants like Amazon's Alexa, Google assistants accompany the proliferation of smart speaker products in the past five years has brought new potentials to provide occupants with a convenient and intuitive interface to interact with smart homes through conversations. Based on IoT, the virtual assistants are able to control a broad range of Wi-Fi connected home devices like thermostats, lighting systems, and security systems. As such, through the simple wake words (e.g., "Alexa", "Hey, Google"), occupants can easily control the home environment with their voice commands. However, the one-way communications in the form of user commands to control building systems do not result in the optimal course of actions. Therefore, in this study, we have envisioned that these virtual assistants, coupled with their corresponding smart home ecosystems could act proactively as a bridge to facilitate human-building interaction and achieve goals like nudging occupants to adopt sustainable and healthy behaviors. A comprehensive data collection was conducted through online surveys, in which 307 valid responses with participant's personal profile information, their perceptions of smart home assistants, and their feedback to our designed messages were collected. The first manuscript compared participants' responses to traditional plain-text energy-saving suggestions and suggestions provided by smart home assistants. The nudging effect of smart home assistants was justified to be significant in affecting occupant's energy-saving behaviors. Occupant's thermal comfort range, smart home device previous experience, values and beliefs were then proved to have significant impact on their intention in taking the smart home assistant's suggestions. The second manuscript fitted 21 personal characteristics features in machine learning models (SVM, Random Forest, Logistic Regression) to predict occupant's intention and attitude towards energy-saving suggestions. The results indicated that occupant's beliefs about interests in taking actions and beliefs about energy expenses, occupant's education level, residence occupancy type, thermal comfort ranges, and smart home device experiences are important features in occupants' energy-saving behavior intention prediction. This research demonstrates the effect of proactive smart home assistants in human-building interaction as well as the impact of personal characteristic features on occupant's energy-saving behaviors, paving a path to the future development of bi-directional human-building communication. Most of this research has focused on households in Western contexts (i.e., Europe and North America), but few studies have explored the design challenges of protecting bystanders, and even fewer have explored these in Muslim Arab Middle Eastern settings, such as Jordan. We conduct 44 interviews with users (i.e., families, domestic workers), local and international business leaders, and smart device designers to explore design challenges for privacy protection in the Jordanian context. Our analysis highlights the importance of considering contextual influences and power dynamics, localization and design guidelines, innovative technologies, awareness to design, and regulation. This paper concludes with recommendations for technical, social, business, and legal interventions to improve data protection design of smart devices in Jordan.</summary><hostname>ACM Digital Library</hostname><publisher>Proc. This paper unpacks the specific ambiguities that make applying the GDPR in this context challenging and identify the key requirements for data controllers in managing data privacy. Methods. This paper takes on a doctrinal approach to research by drawing upon legal sources and existing scholarship in related fields, in particular, legal privacy scholars. Results. The pressing compliance problems stem from the debate on what is considered as 'personal data' in smart buildings in which dictates the compliance requirements, in particular, data protection impact assessments (DPIAs). We identify three facets that smart building controllers should focus on in complying with the GDPR: establishing personal data, identifying individual rights, and determining a high risk to the rights and freedom of natural persons. Conclusions. The law can help prevent harms and ensure that individual rights are protected in smart buildings. raw_output.raw_text: <search query="edge computing smart home security privacy 2023 2024 review" search_time="2026年5月10日10时29分星期日"><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:138"><title>SoK: Privacy-enhancing Smart Home Hubs</title><summary>Smart homes are IoT systems enabling the automation of household operation. The unrestricted collection and processing of data by smart home systems raises legitimate privacy concerns for their users. Over the past decade, there has been significant interest in privacy-enhancing technologies applied at the level of a local smart hub physically located in the home and acting as a gateway between sensors, applications, platform providers, and services in the cloud. The number and variety of projects and research proposals can, however, make their comparison a daunting and unnecessarily complex task. We systematize existing knowledge in this field through the analysis and categorization of 10 industrial and community-contributed systems and 37 research proposals from the literature of the past 11 years. Our results shed light on the diversity of system and trust models considered in the state-of-the-art and on the associated privacy-enhancing technologies. We further identify open research problems and promising approaches that would benefit the smart home hub model and the protection of smart home users’ privacy.</summary><hostname>ResearchGate</hostname><publisher>Proceedings on Privacy Enhancing Technologies</publisher><author_list><author name="Igor Zavalyshyn" affiliation="UCLouvain" /><author name="Axel Legay" affiliation="UCLouvain" /><author name="Annanda Rath" affiliation="Sirris" /><author name="Etienne Rivire" affiliation="UCLouvain" /></author_list><url>https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364083934_SoK_Privacy-enhancing_Smart_Home_Hubs/fulltext/635dab4296e83c26eb650fe2/SoK-Privacy-enhancing-Smart-Home-Hubs.pdf</url><publish_time>2022年6月16日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:139"><title>KNOWLEDGE-BASED CYBER PHYSICAL SECURITY AT SMART HOME: A REVIEW</title><summary>Smart home systems represent the future of modern building infrastructure, integrating numerous devices and applications to elevate the overall quality of life. These systems establish connectivity among smart devices, leveraging network technologies and algorithmic control to monitor and manage the physical environment. However, ensuring robust security in smart homes, alongside securing the smart devices themselves, presents a formidable challenge. A substantial part of security solutions for smart homes rely on data-driven approaches (e.g., machine/deep learning) to identify and mitigate potential threats. These approaches involve training models on extensive datasets, distinguishing them from knowledge-driven methods. In this survey, we delve into the role of knowledge within smart homes, focusing on understanding and reasoning about various events and their utility towards securing smart homes. We propose a taxonomy to characterise the categorisation of decision-making approaches. By specifying the most common vulnerabilities, attacks, and threats, we are able to analyse and assess the countermeasures against them. We have also examined how smart homes have been evaluated in the reviewed papers. Furthermore, we explore the challenges inherent to smart homes and investigate existing solutions that aim to overcome these limitations. Finally, we take a look at key smart home security research gaps while defining future research directions of knowledge-driven schemes.</summary><hostname>Internet of Things Garage</hostname><author_list><author name="Azhar A Alsufyani" affiliation="School of Computer Science and Informatics, Cardiff University, UK" /><author name="Omar Rana" affiliation="School of Computer Science and Informatics, Cardiff University, UK" /><author name="Charith Perera" affiliation="School of Computer Science and Informatics, Cardiff University, UK" /></author_list><url>https://ngcharithperera.gitlab.io/publications/pdfs/Alsufyani2023.pdf</url><publish_time>2023年10月31日0时0分</publish_time

problem: Research Topic: Crafting Techniques for Non-Alcoholic Cocktails. Objective: Investigate current non-alcoholic cocktails to discover innovative production methods and formulations.
final_response:

<answer>Structuring the report around market context, formulation/innovation, preservation/shelf-life, and packaging practices, with data-driven insights and citations.

I. Market Growth and Category Positioning
- The non-alcoholic RTD cocktail segment is among the fastest-growing in the no/low category, with volume increasing 267% from 2023 to 2024 in key markets and expected to rise another 27% over the next four years, far outpacing full-strength cocktails <cite id="call_868042e920d6-1"></cite>.
- Broader non-alcoholic canned and bottled cocktails reached US$7.46 billion in 2023 and are projected to grow to US$26.85 billion by 2032 at a compound annual rate, underscoring the category’s commercial momentum <cite id="call_868042e920d6-0"></cite>.
- Non-alcoholic RTDs (including cocktails) benefit from a larger market backdrop: the non-alcoholic beverage industry is forecast to grow from US$1.22 trillion in 2023 to US$1.99 trillion by 2030 at a 7.4% CAGR, reflecting shifting consumer preferences toward health, wellness, and convenience <cite id="call_868042e920d6-3"></cite>.

II. Formulation and Innovation Practices
A. Ingredient Trends
- Clean-label and functional directions are prominent: many RTD cocktails avoid artificial preservatives and emphasize natural botanicals, stevia, and minimal sweeteners; others incorporate functional ingredients (e.g., adaptogens, vitamins) while maintaining desirable mouthfeel and taste, though formulation requires careful emulsification and stabilization to preserve sensorial properties <cite id="call_4cdc3d2216cc-4"></cite><cite id="call_811510e8c22a-9"></cite>.
- Premiumization and terroir-driven approaches are emerging, with brands using regional botanicals and advanced distillation/maceration to mimic traditional spirits’ complexity without alcohol <cite id="call_4cdc3d2216cc-0"></cite><cite id="call_4cdc3d2216cc-1"></cite>.
- Cold-pressed and fresh-pressed ingredients are used to enhance vibrancy and perceived healthfulness in mocktail-style RTDs, though they require refrigeration and shorter shelf-life management <cite id="call_be80b02e1c7d-0"></cite>.

B. Techniques for Alcohol Removal (when applicable)
- Physical methods dominate commercial RTD cocktail production: vacuum distillation, reverse osmosis, and cold filtration are commonly used to remove alcohol while retaining flavor compounds, with vacuum distillation preferred for delicate botanicals <cite id="call_4cdc3d2216cc-1"></cite><cite id="call_4cdc3d2216cc-4"></cite>.
- Freeze distillation (fractional freezing) is a simpler, home-scale method that enriches flavor by removing ice-rich water, leaving behind a more concentrated liquid; it can be repeated to increase alcohol-free strength but is less precise than industrial methods <cite id="call_2852ad75254f-2"></cite><cite id="call_2852ad75254f-3"></cite>.
- Enzymatic oxidation (e.g., alcohol dehydrogenases) is another enzymatic pathway used to reduce ethanol to acetaldehyde, suitable for mild reductions and often combined with physical methods <cite id="call_f7fa95a3166e-0"></cite>.

C. Case Examples of Craft RTD Cocktail Formulations
- Brands like Tilden use “true cocktail finishes” with bold botanicals, no preservatives, and no added sugar, and recommend refrigeration after opening for up to one month <cite id="call_568678e7095c-3"></cite>.
- Monday Distillery blends distilled botanicals with natural flavors (grapefruit, passionfruit, yuzu), bitters, and sweeteners, and specifies refrigeration post-opening to maintain quality <cite id="call_568678e7095c-1"></cite>.
- Mocktail recipes (e.g., grapekimono with grape juice,菠萝汁, egg white foam, and cream; or a dry-shake egg-white martini) demonstrate how texture and layering can elevate non-alcoholic offerings, often relying on refrigeration for stability <cite id="call_568678e7095c-3"></cite><cite id="call_568678e7095c-4"></cite>.

III. Preservation, Shelf Life, and Storage
A. General Guidelines
- Unopened non-alcoholic beverages typically last 6–12 months in cool, dark storage; non-alcoholic wine may have a longer shelf life (1–2 years), but opened versions degrade within 3–5 days when refrigerated <cite id="call_c0f1c6a15e8a-2"></cite>.
- Specific RTD cocktails vary: canned or bottled RTDs often have 9–12 months shelf life when packaged in oxygen-barrier containers; once opened, carbonated premixed cocktails should be consumed within 24–48 hours, while still cocktails last 3–4 days when refrigerated <cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-0"></cite>.
- Alcohol-free spirits generally last several months unopened and up to one month refrigerated after opening; some premium lines (e.g., JNPR) specify 3–6 months post-opening when refrigerated <cite id="call_c0f1c6a15e8a-3"></cite><cite id="call_c0f1c6a15e8a-1"></cite>.

B. Practical Considerations
- Refrigeration is critical after opening for most RTD cocktails and mixers to slow oxidation, maintain carbonation, and preserve flavor; freezing is generally discouraged as it can cause separation and texture changes <cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-0"></cite><cite id="call_c0f1c6a15e8a-3"></cite>.
- Pasteurization and nitrogen flushing in cans/glass bottles help extend shelf life by reducing microbial risk and oxygen ingress, supporting 9–12 month unopened storage in many RTD formats <cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-0"></cite><cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-1"></cite>.
- Fresh-pressed or dairy-containing mixers (e.g., Bloody Mary bases) should be refrigerated and consumed within 1–3 days to ensure safety and quality <cite id="call_1374f6600510-3"></cite>.

IV. Packaging Strategies
- Oxygen-barrier materials (aluminum cans with advanced linings, nitrogen-flushed bottles) are standard for RTD cocktails to protect against light and oxygen, supporting long shelf lives and maintaining carbonation and flavor <cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-1"></cite><cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-0"></cite>.
- Cold-chain and refrigeration requirements influence labeling and logistics: many RTD cocktails require refrigeration after opening and are often packaged in formats that minimize exposure (cans, bottles with good headspace control) <cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-0"></cite><cite id="call_c0f1c6a15e8a-3"></cite>.
- Consumer education via labels and FAQs is common to clarify storage (e.g., “refrigerate after opening,” “consume within 3–4 days”) and extend product usability <cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-0"></cite><cite id="call_c0f1c6a15e8a-3"></cite>.

V. Recommendations for Crafting Non-Alcoholic Cocktails
- Choose alcohol-removal methods aligned with flavor goals: vacuum distillation or cold filtration for precise, high-quality botanical retention; freeze distillation for simpler, home-scale concentration; enzymatic pathways for mild reductions <cite id="call_4cdc3d2216cc-1"></cite><cite id="call_2852ad75254f-2"></cite><cite id="call_f7fa95a3166e-0"></cite>.
- Use oxygen-barrier packaging and nitrogen flushing where feasible to extend shelf life and maintain carbonation; clearly label refrigeration requirements and estimated post-opening consumption windows <cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-0"></cite><cite id="call_c0f1c6a15e8a-3"></cite>.
- Incorporate clean-label, functional ingredients with emulsification and stabilization strategies to preserve taste and mouthfeel; consider regional botanicals for premium differentiation <cite id="call_811510e8c22a-9"></cite><cite id="call_4cdc3d2216cc-0"></cite>.
- Educate consumers on proper storage (refrigeration after opening) to maximize freshness and safety, especially for mixers containing dairy or fresh-pressed ingredients <cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-0"></cite><cite id="call_1374f6600510-3"></cite>.

VI. Outlook and Opportunities
- The category’s rapid growth suggests strong potential for innovation in clean-label, functional, and premium RTD cocktails; leveraging advanced preservation and packaging can support longer shelf life and broader distribution <cite id="call_868042e920d6-1"></cite><cite id="call_16777b3b33fd-1"></cite>.
- Regional and craft approaches (e.g., cold-pressed bases, local botanicals) can capture niche markets seeking authenticity and health benefits, provided formulation and storage instructions are clearly communicated <cite id="call_be80b02e1c7d-0"></cite><cite id="call_4cdc3d2216cc-0"></cite>.</answer>

Se trata de obtener una bebida sin alcohol con un sabor a mojito, ya sea el clásico mojito, mojito de fresa o de melón. Para ello, el procedimiento consiste en realizar una primera mezcla a la que se añaden azúcar, agua, benzoato sódico, sorbato potásico, emulsión neutra C (5206), Ketrol Rd (Grindsted-X clear supra), goma arábiga, aromatizantes, colorantes, acidulantes, y conservantes, que se mezclan hasta conseguir una mezcla homogénea, tras lo que se añade más agua, azúcar, molienda y dódo cítrico.</summary><hostname>OEPM</hostname><author_list><author name="GARCIA CAMPOY, Asunción" affiliation="25009 MADRID (Madrid) ES" /></author_list><url>http://www.oepm.es/pdf/ES/0000/000/02/64/10/ES-2641054_B1.pdf</url><publish_time>2018年6月20日0时0分</publish_time></document><document reference_id="<|superscript|>:168"><title>INOVASI MINUMAN BERBASIS JAGUNG, SUSU DAN KEJU (JASUKE) DALAM BENTUK MOCKTAIL SEBAGAI ALTERNATIF MINUMAN SEGAR DAN UNIK</title><summary>Puji syukur kehadirat Tuhan Yang Maha Esa atas limpahan rahmat dan karunia-Nya, sehingga penyusunan Tugas Akhir yang berjudul “Inovasi Minuman Berbasis Jagung, Susu dan Keju (Jasuke) Dalam Bentuk Mocktail Sebagai Alternatif Minuman Segar dan Unik” dapat diselesaikan sebagai salah satu syarat dalam menyelesaikan studi pada Program Studi Diploma III Perhotelan Politeknik Harapan Bersama. Penyusunan Tugas Akhir ini tidak lepas dari dukungan dan kontribusi berbagai pihak. Ucapan terimakasih dan penghargaan yang setinggi-tingginya disampaikan pada: 1. Bapak Dr. apt. Heru Nurcahyo, S.Farm., M.Sc. selaku Direktur Politeknik Harapan Bersama. 2. Bapak Lourensius Hendra Putra, S.T., M.M. selaku Ketua Program Studi Diploma III Perhotelan Politeknik Harapan Bersama. 3. problem: Create comprehensive, in-depth study notes for the Diamond Sutra (Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra). These notes should offer deep analysis and interpretation from various perspectives, exploring its teachings and relevance in contexts such as daily life, the workplace/career, business practices, marriage, parenting, emotional well-being, and interpersonal dynamics.
final_response:
<think>
I will produce a comprehensive, structured report on the Diamond Sutra with deep analysis and practical applications across multiple life domains. I will anchor key doctrinal points to scholarly sources on the text’s structure and meaning, and use citations from commentarial and philosophical works to ground the interpretations. I will then translate these insights into actionable principles for daily life, the workplace, business, marriage, parenting, emotional well-being, and interpersonal dynamics.
